title: Process and Creation

description.main: Catalogue of the 2013 centenary exhibition at Tokyo Station Gallery, built around newly found material from the Ueda estate: contact sheets, early postwar colour work, period magazine articles and the last frames in his camera. Supervised by Ryuichi Kaneko, with commentary by Hajime Nariai. Japanese text.
description.extended:
Shoji Ueda: Process and Creation is the catalogue of the centenary exhibition Tokyo Station Gallery mounted in 2013. Its question is how the photographer of the Tottori dunes put each picture together, and how he was formed as a photographer.

Seigensha published the 224-page volume in October 2013 under the Japanese title 植田正治のつくりかた. The photography historian Ryuichi Kaneko supervised it, and the Tokyo Station Gallery curator Hajime Nariai wrote the commentary. Short columns work through material newly found in the Ueda estate. There are contact sheets for well-known dune pictures, the magazine articles in which the work first appeared, colour photographs he attempted soon after the war, and the last frames left in his camera when he died in 2000. The exhibition travelled to the Iwate Museum of Art in 2014; the text is in Japanese.

Ueda (1913–2000) worked all his life in the San'in region of western Japan, posing family, neighbours and children on the dunes near Sakaiminato in a flat, staged manner that came to be called Ueda-cho. The staged work began in 1939, the Sand Dune series ran in Camera in 1949, and Brilliant Scenes (1981) took the method into colour. Tokyo Station Gallery had held his largest lifetime retrospective in 1993; this was its first Ueda show since reopening in 2012.
description.artist_bio: Shoji Ueda (1913-2000), born and based in Sakaiminato, Tottori, made staged black-and-white photographs on the local dunes from 1939; the Sand Dune series appeared in Camera in 1949. Colour series Brilliant Scenes (1981). Chevalier des Arts et des Lettres 1996. Shoji Ueda Museum of Photography, Tottori, opened 1995.
description.exhibition_context: Tokyo Station Gallery's second Ueda exhibition after the 1993 retrospective; the first since the gallery reopened in 2012. Supervised by Ryuichi Kaneko with the cooperation of the Shoji Ueda Office. Toured to the Iwate Museum of Art, 12 April to 8 June 2014.
